newsitem.title: UK: SBC Warburg to set bonds linked to UK house prices.
newsitem.headline: SBC Warburg to set bonds linked to UK house prices.

text.p: SBC Warburg will next week launch the first ever bonds which are backed by mortgages linked to the capital appreciation on British houses, an official there said on Friday.

The deal will total 145 million stg ($245 million), and will be split into a 115.6 million stg floating-rate bond and a 29.3 million stg fixed rate bond. SBC Warburg expected the bonds to have a technical maturity of approximately 75 years but an average life of between eight and 12 years.

The bonds will be securitised by a pool of mortgages marketed by the Bank of Scotland between December 1996 and April 1997. The mortgages, known as Shared Appreciation Mortgages (SAMs), offer homeowners the chance to trade subsidised mortgage repayments for a share in any capital appreciation that accrues to them on selling their homes.
Co-Head of SBC Warburg's global residential property markets Craig Corn told Reuters that the bonds were aimed at pension funds, insurance companies and fund managers.
"The bond is interesting because it has the characteristics of debt, equity and property, so many different parts of institution's portfolios are looking at it," Corn said.
Pension funds will also be attracted by the bonds as "it is an interesting way to hedge their long term liabilities because of the strong relationship between house prices and earnings", Corn said.
SBC Warburg expected the Bank of Scotland to look for further securitisation by the end of the year on SAMs which they have been marketing since May.
The bond issues next week have a AAAr rating from Standard & Poor's credit rating agency.
-- Chris Young, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7970 ($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
